2026-11-c20.p: The following is the process of finding the value of $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{12}a_k+\sum_{k=1}^{5}a_{2k+1}$.

box: For every natural number $n\ge 2$, since $a_{n+1}=\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n+1}a_k-\sum_{k=1}^{n}a_k$,
$\qquad a_{n+1}=\dfrac{2}{3}\left(a_{n+1}-a_n\right)+\boxed{\ (\text{A})\ }$,
and rearranging this gives
$\qquad 2a_n+a_{n+1}=3\times\boxed{\ (\text{A})\ }\qquad\cdots\cdots$ ①
Substituting $n=2$ into both sides of $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}a_k=\frac{2}{3}a_n+\frac{1}{6}n^{2}-\frac{1}{6}n+10\ (n\ge 2)$ gives
$\qquad a_2=\boxed{\ (\text{B})\ }\qquad\cdots\cdots$ ②
By ① and ②,
$\qquad \displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{12}a_k+\sum_{k=1}^{5}a_{2k+1}=a_1+a_2+\sum_{k=1}^{5}\left(2a_{2k+1}+a_{2k+2}\right)=\boxed{\ (\text{C})\ }$

Therefore, if $R$ is the radius of the circumcircle of triangle $\mathrm{BPC}$, then by the law of sines in triangle $\mathrm{BPC}$, $R=\boxed{\ (\text{C})\ }$.

box: Since all real roots of the equation $f(x)=x$ are $0$ and $3$, finding the real roots of $f\big(f(x)\big)=f(x)$ is the same as finding the real roots of $f(x)\times\big(f(x)-3\big)=0$.
For $0\le x<4$, all real roots of $f(x)\times\big(f(x)-3\big)=0$ are $0$, $\boxed{\ (\text{A})\ }$, $3$, so

Also, since $f(x+4)=f(x)$ for every real number $x$, the three sequences $\{a_{3n-2}\}$, $\{a_{3n-1}\}$, $\{a_{3n}\}$ are arithmetic sequences with first terms $0$, $\boxed{\ (\text{A})\ }$, $3$, respectively, and common difference $\boxed{\ (\text{B})\ }$ for all three.
